articles.title: When to Self-Host LightOnOCR-3 vs. Calling a Hosted PDF-to-Markdown API
articles.excerpt: When an AI agent or RAG pipeline needs to turn a PDF into clean Markdown, teams hit a practical fork: run an open-weight OCR model on their own GPU, or pay per page for a hosted conversion API. LightO…
articles.body: When an AI agent or RAG pipeline needs to turn a PDF into clean Markdown, teams hit a practical fork: run an open-weight OCR model on their own GPU, or pay per page for a hosted conversion API. LightOnAI's October 8, 2026 release of LightOnOCR-3 ( 0.8B , 1B , and 4B Apache-2.0 checkpoints) makes the tradeoffs concrete. The 0.8B and 4B models move onto Qwen3.5 vision-language backbones and post strong numbers on clean technical layouts, while exposing the exact places where self-hosting stops being free. What LightOnOCR-3's benchmarks show Across olmOCR-Bench , ParseBench , and fr-bench-pdf2md (leaderboard revision 3576c52 ), LightOnOCR-3-0.8B scores 85.5 overall on olmOCR-Bench , hitting 90.8 on tables, 89.6 on arXiv math, 85.2 on multi-column text, and 94.1 on long tiny text.

articles.title: CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md: Which Claude Code Reads
articles.excerpt: Originally published on DevToolHub. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md first and falls back to AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md exists. That one rule settles most claude.md vs agents.md questions. If you als…
articles.body: Originally published on DevToolHub . Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md first and falls back to AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md exists. That one rule settles most claude.md vs agents.md questions. If you also use Codex, Cursor or Copilot, put the shared rules in AGENTS.md and add a CLAUDE.md that imports it with @AGENTS.md . I tested this on Claude Code 2.1.322. I put a unique codeword in each file, ran claude -p in throwaway folders, and asked it to list every codeword in its loaded instructions. The results match the docs, with one catch that most guides skip: a CLAUDE.local.md quietly switches AGENTS.md off. What Is the Difference Between CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md? CLAUDE.md is Claude Code's own instruction file.

articles.body: Most advice about removing a logo from a video assumes the logo sits in a corner you do not need. The suggestion runs: crop the frame, scale it back up, and the problem disappears along with a strip of the picture. That works exactly once. The moment the overlay drifts toward the centre of the frame, or the subject's shoulder passes behind it, cropping stops being an option and the work becomes something else: you have to reconstruct the pixels that were covered. That distinction is worth taking seriously, because it decides which tools can help you at all. What the overlay actually destroys A watermark replaces real image data.

articles.body: A GitHub awesome list looks like a straightforward place to share a useful product. Find a relevant section, add a line and open a pull request. articles.title: 🚨 Got a 169.254 IP Address? It's DHCP, Not Your Wi-Fi
articles.excerpt: "It says connected, but there's no internet." 😩 You check the IP, and it starts with 169.254. Good news: that one number already told you most of the story. When a Windows PC joins a network, it asks…
articles.body: "It says connected, but there's no internet." 😩 You check the IP, and it starts with 169.254 . Good news: that one number already told you most of the story. 🕵️ What 169.254 actually means When a Windows PC joins a network, it asks a DHCP server for an IP address, gateway, and DNS servers. If nobody answers, Windows gives itself an APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing) address in the 169.254.0.0/16 range. That address can't reach the internet or your company network.

articles.title: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027

articles.body: Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities.

articles.title: Astronomers stunned after James Webb Space Telescope discovers the earliest pair of black hole-powered quasars
articles.excerpt: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist!
articles.body: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of supermassive black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist! The compact quasar pair, spotted with the aid of the Gemini North telescope, has been designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, which means "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe." The compact quasar pair is seen as it was 900 million years after the Big Bang at a time when such supermassive black holes should not have had time to grow to such tremendous masses. Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua isn't just the oldest and most distant quasar pairing ever seen.
articles.author: Robert Lea

articles.title: SpaceX launches 2nd mystery mission for US Space Force in 6-day span (video, photos)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California tonight (Nov. 11), the second such mission for the company in a six-day span.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California tonight (Nov. 11), the second such flight for the company in a six-day span. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:36 p.m. EST (8:36 p.m. local California time; 0136 GMT on Nov. 12), kicking off a mission called USSF-627. Vandenberg hosted a similar liftoff less than a week ago: On Nov. 6, a Falcon 9 sent the USSF-432 mission skyward from the site, which lies on California's gorgeous but often foggy central coast. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-627 mission for the U.S. Space Force from California on Nov. 11, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) We don't know much about USSF-627 or USSF-432; both are classified.

Moon, Venus and Spica Meet Explanation: Not all those who wander are lost. A night sky example is that planets wander, and in fact the very word “planet” comes from “wandering star” in Greek. As planets shift relative to fixed stars , they may appear from our perspective to get closer to other astronomical objects. Such meetings are called conjunctions . They don’t happen by chance, but follow the precise laws of celestial mechanics .
